d: The world's three biggest nuclear powers are preparing for an unprecedented meeting in Shenzhen. Donald Trump, Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin are expected to meet on November 19, 2026, as Washington pushes for a new nuclear arms-control agreement. But China is refusing to play by America's rules. With an estimated 620 nuclear warheads, Beijing has a much smaller arsenal than the United States and Russia. Yet China is expanding rapidly, adding around 100 warheads annually since 2023.
